priceSnapshot.note: Read this against a FORTY-TWO HOUR blind window, not a normal six-hour session. Neither the 2026-08-24 midnight nor the morning run executed, and 2026-08-23 produced no sessions at all, so the last desk mark is the 2026-08-22 endday at 77,283.3 taken 19:34 COT Saturday. Everything below is measured against that. In between BTC did two large things in sequence. FIRST it broke down: the 05:00Z hour on 23 August traded 75,559.5, which is 955.5 points BELOW the 76,515.0 shelf that four consecutive reports had named as the reduce trigger and that had never once closed through. It closed through. SECOND it reversed and ran 5.88 percent off that low to tag 79,999.8 in the 15:00Z hour today - two tenths of a point short of the 80,000 handle - and was rejected there. Spot now sits 79,017.8: up 2.24 percent on the Saturday mark, up 4.58 percent on the Sunday low, and 982.0 points (1.23 percent) below today's high. changePct 2.15 is measured against OKX open24h of 77,352.6. The sessionRange below is the FULL window since the last desk mark, which is why it is 4,440.3 points wide rather than the few hundred a normal midday reports.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $77,860.0 - the low of the 13:00Z hour, which is the exact candle that launched the impulse from 77,860.0 to 79,999.8. This is the springboard, not a decoration: the 1H EMA50 sits 366.8 points beneath it at 77,493.20, so a settled close below 77,860.0 puts price back inside the pre-breakout book with the next real EMA support already behind it. Spot is 1,157.8 points above it, which is 1.57 hourly ATRs at the current 736.39 - one ordinary hour does not reach it, two bad ones do. Note the FIRST warning sits higher, at 78,500.0: that is the heaviest realized long-liquidation bucket of the day (2.72m across 248 fills, 96 percent longs) and it is only 0.70 hourly ATRs below spot, so it is ordinary noise distance and does NOT qualify as a trigger on its own. Trigger is a settled CLOSE, never a wick - that distinction is the only reason the desk was not shaken out at 76,515.0 twice last week.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $80,120.0. This gate is placed 120.2 points ABOVE the 79,999.8 rejection high DELIBERATELY, applying this desk's own logged lesson from 2026-08-22 midday: an add gate placed at the exact high of the session that produced it gets wicked, not confirmed. That lesson has now been proven twice - morning set 77,519.1 and the tape ran 54.3 points through it and closed back below; midday then set 77,573.4 and the session never reached it at all. So this run refuses to put the gate on the wick. 80,120.0 also sits above the 80,000 round number AND above the 1.05m of realized SHORT liquidations clustered there, meaning a settled close through it is a level that has already consumed the resting short leverage rather than one that merely touched it.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from TAKE_PROFIT (Saturday's first trim, 10 percent of the core at 77,283.3) to TAKE_PROFIT again - a SECOND trim, 8 percent, at 79,031.2. Repeat verb, different trade: 1,747.9 points higher, a 2.26 percent better fill, and the first action this desk has taken with the daily RSI at the highest reading of the entire advance. State the unusual book condition plainly, because it shaped the size. The scheduled sessions COLLIDED: midnight never ran, and a morning run fired at 13:20 COT minutes before this report, deploying 18 USDT into the core at 78,990.4 and lifting it to 0.0020782 BTC at an average of 72,105.81 while cutting free cash to 64.78. That left the wallet 71.7 percent invested at a price 12.52 percent above the daily EMA20. This trim rebalances rather than reverses, and the arithmetic is the point: after it the core is 0.00191194 BTC, still LARGER than the 0.00185032 carried on Saturday, with cash back to 77.69. The desk ends the session longer than it started the weekend and 92 percent exposed to any continuation. Three things changed materially since Saturday. FIRST, the 76,515.0 reduce gate FIRED - the 05:00Z hour on 23 August closed through it - and the desk was not present to act, so the record logs a fired trigger with no execution. SECOND, compression resolved exactly as Saturday warned: hourly ATR expanded 51.2 percent from 486.95 to 736.39, going DOWN to 75,559.5 first and UP to 79,999.8 second, which is why the Saturday trim reads as lost upside rather than protection. THIRD, positioning got genuinely cleaner - the long/short account ratio fell 1.17 to 1.01 and funding is 0.0077 percent per eight hours, so the froth flagged on Saturday was flushed at 75,559.5 rather than carried higher. That refutation is precisely why this trim is 8 percent and not larger. stopOrder stays NOT recommended: the next report is roughly six hours away with the desk awake for it, and the remainder is a long-term spot core that should not carry a hard stop. 77,860.0 is where one would sit.

liquidation.note: The heaviest bucket of the window by a clear margin: 2.72m across 248 separate fills, and 96 percent of it was LONGS. It sits 517.8 points below spot, which is 0.70 hourly ATRs - inside ordinary noise distance. Read it correctly: this is REALIZED liquidation, an autopsy of where leverage actually died between 12:50Z and 18:17Z today, not a forward book of resting orders. It matters because leverage rebuilds where it was just cleared, and because 78,500 is also the approximate base of the 13:00Z impulse leg, so two independent things point at the same handle.

1.97m over 154 fills, 92 percent longs. Together with 78,500 and 78,750 this forms a 6.30m long-heavy shelf spanning 78,250 to 78,750 - the single densest zone in the window and all of it beneath spot.
1.61m over 181 fills, 91 percent longs. The upper edge of the long-flush shelf and the first of the three the tape would reach on a pullback.

0.71m over just 32 fills - the smallest fill count in the top group, meaning a few large positions rather than many small ones - and 100 percent longs. It sits essentially on the 77,860.0 reduce line, which is a mild confirmation that the springboard is where size actually died.

1.30m over 204 fills and almost perfectly two-sided at 47 percent longs to 53 percent shorts. Spot is sitting on this handle right now (79,017.8), which is exactly what a two-sided bucket means: this is the price both books are being liquidated at, i.e. the current fight, not a magnet.
1.46m over 176 fills and 100 percent SHORTS - not one long died here. The nearest magnet above, 732.2 points away or 0.99 hourly ATRs. This is where the squeeze into 80,000 actually happened.

1.05m over 158 fills, again 100 percent shorts. The round number did its job twice: it cleared the short leverage AND it rejected price to the tenth of a point (session high 79,999.8). That is why the add gate is at 80,120.0 and not here.

liquidityMagnet.note: pull is DOWN, and the arithmetic rather than the feel says so: 6.30m of long-heavy liquidation sits in the 78,250-78,750 shelf below spot against 2.50m of short-heavy liquidation at 79,750-80,000 above, a 2.5-to-1 imbalance in favour of the downside cluster. A realized cluster is evidence of where stops lived, not proof that they still do. The forward-looking read is that both books were cut today - 7.82m of longs and 5.54m of shorts across 5.4 hours - so this is a two-sided flush, not a one-way trap, and the down-pull is a lean rather than a thesis.

atr.source: Computed in-browser from the last 300 OKX 1H BTC-USDT bars using Wilder true range (max of high-low, abs(high - prior close), abs(low - prior close)), seeded on the first 14 true ranges and smoothed forward. 736.39 against 486.95 at Saturday's endday - a 51.2 percent EXPANSION. This is the single cleanest confirmation of a prior call in the record: Saturday's report wrote that hourly range had contracted for three straight sessions and that 'compression this persistent usually resolves with expansion rather than more of the same'. It did, within thirty hours, and it expanded in BOTH directions - down 1,723.8 points to 75,559.5, then up 4,440.3 to 79,999.8. pct = 736.39 / 79,017.8 = 0.93 percent.

calibration.rollingRecord: First session in forty-two hours, and the schedule broke in both directions. Two of the four scheduled runs before this one did not execute (2026-08-24 midnight and morning at their windows) and 2026-08-23 produced none at all, so the 76,515.0 reduce trigger fired with nobody at the desk. Then the catch-up run fired late: a morning session executed at 13:20 COT, minutes before this midday report, and both traded the same book.
calibration.note: Be blunt about this run, because two things went wrong and only one of them was a judgement error. FIRST, THE GATE FIRED AND NOBODY WAS THERE. Saturday's endday set reduce at 76,515.0 and the 05:00Z hour on 23 August traded 75,559.5 - 955.5 points clean through it, not a wick - and closed below. Four consecutive reports had named that shelf and it finally broke. priorReduceFired is therefore TRUE, but no reduction was executed against it because neither the midnight nor the morning session ran. That is an infrastructure failure, not an analytical one, and it is the more important of the two: a trigger that fires into an empty chair is worth nothing. SECOND, THE TRIM WAS EARLY. Saturday sold 10 percent of the spot core at 77,283.3 and spot is now 79,017.8, so that trim gave up 1,734.5 points of upside on roughly 0.000206 BTC, about 0.36 USDT. acting_helped is FALSE on outcome. But mark the reasoning honestly rather than just the score: Saturday's explicit warning was that three sessions of ATR compression 'usually resolves with expansion' - and ATR expanded 51.2 percent within thirty hours. The direction call inside that expansion was wrong; the volatility call was exactly right. THIRD, one of Saturday's four stated reasons to trim has now been REFUTED by the tape: it flagged the long/short account ratio climbing to 1.17 as evidence longs were crowding into a stalling market. That crowding was flushed at 75,559.5 and the ratio is 1.01 today. The positioning argument for caution no longer exists, which is precisely why this run's second trim is sized at only 8 percent, and why the overall bias is bullish despite taking profit.
